report:
Conclusion
- The finetuning did not produce any meaningful, localized representational change. In other words: there is no clear finetuning objective / domain shift that I can detect from these signals — Model B is effectively the same as Model A (or only trivially changed).

Reasoning from the evidence
- Difference norms are all zero (or below measurement resolution) at every layer and token position. That indicates there is no concentrated residual-stream change anywhere in the network for the sample set — i.e., no strong learned behavior sitting in particular layers/positions.
- The logit-lens results were produced after RMS-normalizing the tiny difference vectors. Normalization forces a direction even when the magnitude is negligible; the top tokens returned are simply the highest-frequency / function tokens in the vocabulary (' o', 'is', 'it', ' p', ' t', '\n', 'in', ' a', 'or', ' s'). That pattern is what you expect from noise or an uninformative direction, not from a meaningful finetuning objective (which would show semantically coherent, targeted tokens).
- Patchscope readouts show no noticeable continuations (no signalful outputs reported), consistent with the norms being essentially zero.

Most likely explanations
- No substantive finetuning (the finetune run was a no-op), or finetuning strength was extremely small so that representational differences are beneath detection thresholds.
- Alternatively, the finetuning could have been something global and subtle (e.g., tiny temperature-like smoothing or tiny reweighting toward very high-frequency tokens), but the measurements here do not show any meaningful, directed change beyond generic high-frequency token bias caused by normalizing noise.

Suggested follow-ups to confirm
- Measure raw (non-normalized) difference magnitudes on a larger, more diverse corpus and with higher numeric precision to confirm the differences are truly negligible.
- Run behavioral tests (e.g., prompts targeting a suspected objective) to see if there are measurable output differences in probability distributions or generations.
- Inspect parameter deltas (weights/biases) directly to see whether the finetune modified parameters appreciably.

Short answer: no identifiable finetuning objective — Model B appears essentially unchanged from Model A (or only trivially nudged toward very-high-frequency tokens).
